note: Fixture rubric whose criteria use DIFFERENT behavioral scales (0..3 and 0..7). Both other fixture rubrics are uniform (3x0..5, 2x0..10), and a uniform rubric's mean always lands on an integer percentage — which is exactly why the verdict rounding defect survived 874 tests. Approved for the test suite only; the sources are synthetic, so there is no real expertise here to launder.

statement.value: Cut every clause the reader could supply from context.
statement.warrant: Vega states the cut as an imperative over inferable clauses; this restates it in the second person without narrowing what counts as inferable.

evidence.phrase: Trim every clause the reader can infer from context

guidance.value: Judge what the surrounding text already establishes, not what a first-time reader might miss in isolation. A clause restating an established fact is the clearest case.
guidance.warrant: Vega ties the test to what the reader can supply, which is a property of context, not of the sentence alone; 'judge against the surrounding text' is the operational reading of that.

evidence.phrase: A sentence should carry only what the reader cannot supply alone

statement.value: Vary sentence length so tempo tracks what the moment needs.
statement.warrant: Two sources state the two directions — short runs quicken, a long sentence slows — and this joins them into the single control they describe without adding a rule about when to use which.

evidence.phrase: A run of short sentences quickens the pace
A single long sentence slows the tempo

guidance.value: Look for length changing WITH the scene's demands, not merely changing. Uniform length is the failure; random variation is not the fix.
guidance.warrant: Both sources pair a length with an effect, which makes the effect the criterion; variation with no matching demand satisfies neither statement.
